description: Curated research map. Directed arrows indicate study-reported pathway relationships, not necessarily direct physical binding. Context and evidence level are mandatory.

nodes.label: PROX1
nodes.summary: A transcription factor whose transfer from neurons into Müller glia was implicated in suppressing regeneration in mouse retina.
nodes.boundary: Global PROX1 inhibition is not supported.

nodes.label: ASCL1
nodes.summary: A proneural transcription factor experimentally used with chromatin modulation to reprogram adult mouse Müller glia.
nodes.boundary: The cited study did not test ASCL1 together with PROX1 blockade.

nodes.label: Glial reprogramming
nodes.summary: Entry of Müller glia into a progenitor or neuronal differentiation program. Different studies use different interventions and assays.
nodes.boundary: Neuronal marker expression alone does not establish repaired human vision.

nodes.label: Dual strategy?
nodes.summary: Untested research question: would perturbing PROX1 transfer and using ASCL1-based reprogramming produce complementary effects?
nodes.boundary: No supplied paper demonstrated the combination. This is NOT a known protein–protein interaction.

nodes.label: FGF2 + GSK3 inhibition
nodes.summary: Combined laboratory conditions discussed in a 2026 preprint on cultures of adult human donor retina.
nodes.boundary: Preprint and ex-vivo tissue only; not evidence of restored vision.

nodes.label: Neural-lineage markers
nodes.summary: Preliminary markers of neural-lineage commitment reported in adult human retinal cultures.
nodes.boundary: Markers are not an established functional replacement neuron or clinical benefit.

nodes.label: PTEN
nodes.summary: Growth-control regulator that negatively regulates the mTOR pathway; also an important tumor suppressor.
nodes.boundary: Systemic or permanent loss is unsafe to infer as a treatment.

nodes.label: SOCS3
nodes.summary: Negative regulator of cytokine/JAK–STAT signaling in the cited mouse optic nerve work.
nodes.boundary: The mouse combination result does not establish human optic nerve recovery.

nodes.label: mTOR signaling
nodes.summary: Pathway upregulated when PTEN restraint is removed; associated with growth responses in retinal ganglion cells.
nodes.boundary: Activation of growth signaling is not the same as correctly wiring axons.

nodes.label: STAT3 signaling
nodes.summary: Signaling pathway promoted after SOCS3 deletion, involved in sustained axon growth in the cited mouse model.
nodes.boundary: The cited experiment does not establish a human clinical therapy.

nodes.label: Sustained axon growth
nodes.summary: Mouse optic nerve axon regrowth reported after combined PTEN and SOCS3 deletion.
nodes.boundary: Regrowth is not proof of full correct reconnection or human vision restoration.

nodes.label: YAP1
nodes.summary: Mechanotransduction regulator acting upstream of wound-associated Engrailed-1 activation in mouse fibroblasts.
nodes.boundary: YAP has different tissue roles; blanket inhibition is not justified.

nodes.label: EN1 activation
nodes.summary: Activation of the Engrailed-1 program distinguishes scar-producing fibroblast lineages in the cited mouse experiments.
nodes.boundary: Cell lineage participation is not identical to a direct chemical interaction.

nodes.label: Scar-associated lineage
nodes.summary: Engrailed-1-positive fibroblast lineage contributes to skin scarring after mechanical cues in mice.
nodes.boundary: No proven scar-free human treatment follows directly.

nodes.label: MSTN / myostatin
nodes.summary: Normal skeletal muscle growth regulator. Human loss-of-function genetics supports an inhibitory role.
nodes.boundary: Increased muscle mass does not necessarily improve strength or regenerate damaged muscle.

nodes.label: Muscle mass
nodes.summary: Marked muscle hypertrophy was documented in a human with biallelic MSTN loss-of-function.
nodes.boundary: A single genetic case does not establish safe benefit from treatment.

edges.model: Mouse retina, injury and degeneration models
edges.finding: Transferred PROX1 was reported to restrict retinal Müller glia reprogramming; extracellular sequestration relieved that restraint.
edges.limit: Not proof of a working treatment in humans.

edges.finding: ASCL1 combined with an HDAC inhibitor supported generation of neuron-like cells with reported functional features.
edges.limit: Not studied here in combination with PROX1 manipulation.

edges.finding: A possible complementary intervention is proposed by comparing separate mouse studies, not by measuring a combined intervention.
edges.limit: No demonstrated PROX1–ASCL1 direct binding, synergy, or human benefit.

edges.finding: Conceptual overlap in glial reprogramming motivates a research question.
edges.limit: No published combination outcome established here.

edges.model: Cultured adult human donor retina ex vivo; preprint
edges.finding: An unreviewed 2026 manuscript reports proliferation and neural-lineage marker changes following culture interventions.
edges.limit: Not peer-reviewed, no demonstrated living-human vision restoration.

edges.finding: The cited study identifies PTEN as a negative regulator of mTOR signaling in adult retinal ganglion cells.
edges.limit: Pathway relation is not necessarily direct molecular binding.

edges.finding: The cited study identifies SOCS3 as a negative regulator of JAK/STAT signaling.
edges.limit: Pathway regulation does not require direct SOCS3–STAT3 binding.

edges.model: Mouse optic nerve crush, joint PTEN/SOCS3 deletion
edges.finding: Combined pathway activation was reported alongside stronger sustained axon growth after dual deletion.
edges.limit: Neither a direct pathway-to-neuron physical interaction nor human treatment evidence.

edges.model: Mouse optic nerve crush, joint PTEN/SOCS3 deletion
edges.finding: Activation of STAT3 alongside mTOR was implicated in sustained regrowth after combined deletion.
edges.limit: This line does not imply that STAT3 alone explains the combined effect.

edges.model: Mouse dermal fibroblasts and wound models
edges.finding: Blocking fibroblast YAP signaling reduced activation of Engrailed-1 and favored regenerative wound healing in mice.
edges.limit: Tissue-specific signaling, not proof that general YAP blockade is safe.

edges.finding: EN1-positive fibroblast lineage was reported to contribute to scar formation.
edges.limit: Lineage association must not be described as a direct protein binding event.

edges.finding: A human case report associated inherited myostatin loss-of-function with pronounced muscle hypertrophy.
edges.limit: Does not demonstrate muscle healing or clinical utility of a myostatin-blocking drug.
